core_obligations: Part (1) (proof lines 12231-12248): using the collection B of quasi-compact and quasi-separated objects, the author writes an arbitrary sheaf of sets as the filtered colimit of its restrictions to the members of B, each of which is constructible because the scheme is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
Part (3) (proof lines 12251-12266): for a Noetherian ring the author uses the description of a sheaf of modules as a filtered colimit of finite type sheaves and then of constructible ones.
Part (2) (proof lines 12269-12273): for a torsion abelian sheaf the author writes F as the union of its n-torsion subsheaves and reduces to the bounded torsion case, where the previous parts apply.
proof_roadmap: Write a sheaf of sets as a filtered colimit of constructible pieces over the quasi-compact quasi-separated objects.
For modules over a Noetherian ring, use the finite type approximation.
For torsion abelian sheaves, filter by n-torsion and reduce to the earlier parts.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that on a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme every sheaf of sets, every torsion abelian sheaf and every sheaf of modules over a Noetherian ring is a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves (statement lines 12215-12229). The proof treats the three parts separately: the case of sheaves of sets uses the approximation by restrictions to quasi-compact and quasi-separated objects (proof lines 12231-12248), the module case uses the approximation by finite type sheaves (proof lines 12251-12266), and the torsion abelian case is reduced to the bounded torsion situation through the n-torsion filtration (proof lines 12269-12273). The non-formal content is the choice of the approximating systems. The claim is H2: three approximations, each written out.
